intro.text: The Davey Tree Expert Company, which was founded in 1880 and incorporated in Ohio in 1909, and its subsidiaries provide a wide range of arboricultural, horticultural, environmental and consulting services to our customers throughout the United States and Canada. We have two reportable operating segments organized by type or class of customer: Residential and Commercial, and Utility. Our Residential and Commercial segment provides services to our residential and commercial customers including: the treatment, preservation, maintenance, removal and planting of trees, shrubs and other plant life; the practice of landscaping, grounds maintenance, tree surgery, tree feeding and tree spraying; the application of fertilizer, herbicides and insecticides; and natural resource management and consulting, forestry research and development, and environmental planning.

oi.text: The fair values of the reporting units were estimated using discounted projected cash flows for the goodwill impairment analysis that required assumptions related to revenues, operating margins, growth rates, discount rates, and working capital requirements. In determining those assumptions, we consider data for each reporting unit, including its annual budget for the upcoming year, its longer-term performance expectations, anticipated future cash flows and market data. Assumptions were also made for perpetual growth rates for periods beyond the forecast period. The assumptions used to calculate the fair value of a reporting unit may change from year to year based on operating results, market conditions and other factors. Changes in these assumptions could materially affect the determination of the fair value for each reporting unit.

opex.text: Operating Expenses --Operating expenses of $1,301,601 increased $113,044 from the prior year, and as a percentage of revenues increased to 66.8% from 64.6%. Utility Services increased $49,294, or 6.6%, from 2024, and as a percentage of revenues increased to 74.8% from 74.0%. The increase was attributable to increases in labor and benefits expenses, subcontractor expenses and materials expenses. Residential and Commercial Services increased $31,594, or 7.2%, compared with 2024 and as a percentage of revenue increased to 53.4% from 53.2%. The increase was primarily attributable to increases in labor and benefits expense, subcontractor expenses, materials expenses and equipment expenses partially offset by a decrease in professional services expenses. The remaining increase from prior year was primarily attributable to a one-time $34,500 increase in self insurance related expenses driven by specific large loss claims within our general liability and vehicle liability classifications.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During 2025, we had revenues of approximately $167 million, or approximately 9% of total revenues, from Pacific Gas & Electric Company ("PG&E"), our largest customer.
One utility customer approximated 9 % of revenues during 2025, 9 % in 2024 and 10 % in 2023.

Our long-term success partially depends on our ability to attract and retain key employees who possess the experience, leadership capabilities and values necessary to support our business and execute our strategy.

Competition for the best people can be intense, and depends on many factors, including the attractiveness of our compensation and benefit programs, and we may not be able to promote, hire or retain key employees.
We rely on the accuracy, capacity and security of our information technology systems.
We depend on such parties to implement adequate controls and safeguards to protect against and report cyber incidents.
Even though we primarily sell our services to U.S. customers and our suppliers are primarily domestic, we still rely on imported materials, components, or finished goods.

The ultimate impact of tariffs and other trade policies on the Company's business will depend on several factors, including future measures implemented by the U.S. government and the governments of other countries, the overall magnitude and duration of those measures, and the Company's ability to mitigate effects.
Share repurchases may be made from time to time and the timing of any repurchases and the actual number of shares repurchased will depend on a variety of factors.

We have generally been able to offset increases in these costs through various productivity and cost reduction initiatives, as well as adjusting our prices to pass through some of these higher costs to our customers; however, our ability to raise our prices depends on market conditions and competitive dynamics.
Cash generated from operations, our revolving credit facility and note issuances are our primary sources of capital.
The 15 % discount of total shares purchased under the plan resulted in compensation cost recognized of $ 2,383 in 2025, $ 2,073 in 2024 and $ 1,712 in 2023.
